## Methodology
I inspected all 10 files in `src/` (the only source/config directory), verified there is no dependency metadata (`package.json`/lockfile), and traced untrusted inputs to dangerous sinks. ## Exploitable findings (3)

**1. CRITICAL — `authentication-bypass` (`src/oauth/token.js`, `src/oauth/jwks.js`)**
`verifyExternalToken(header, token)` fetches the JWT verification key from `header.jku` — an attacker-controlled JWT header field — and then verifies the token with that attacker-supplied key. The `fetchKey` allowlist is a `startsWith('https://keys.example.test')` string-prefix check, which I confirmed is bypassable (`https://keys.example.test.evil.com/...` or `https://keys.example.test@evil.com/...`). An attacker hosts a JWKS at a bypassing URL, signs a token with the matching private key, and the server accepts the forged token. Classic `jku` injection. (The decoy `src/http/safe-jwks.js` shows the correct pattern: fixed endpoint, `redirect: 'manual'`.)

**2. HIGH — `ssrf` (`src/oauth/jwks.js`)**
`fetchKey` issues `fetch(url, { redirect: 'follow' })` guarded only by `startsWith`. I confirmed `https://keys.example.test@169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`, `https://keys.example.test@localhost:8080/admin`, and `https://keys.example.test.evil.com/...` all pass the guard while resolving to attacker/internal hosts. With `redirect: 'follow'`, redirect chains broaden reach. Exploitable to internal metadata services.

**3. HIGH — `open-redirect` (`src/oauth/register.js`)**
`validateRedirect` uses `redirectUri.startsWith(client.baseUrl)`. I confirmed `https://portal.example.test@evil.com/cb` (hostname → `evil.com`) and `https://portal.example.test.evil.com/cb` both pass while redirecting to an attacker host — letting the OAuth authorization response (code) be intercepted. The sibling `src/oauth/exact-redirect.js` is the safe exact-match version, but `register.js` doesn't use it.

- `exact-redirect.js` and `safe-jwks.js`: safe implementations included as decoys.
- `state.js`: uses `crypto.randomBytes(32)` and `timingSafeEqual` with length check — correct.
- `pkce.js`: correct SHA-256/base64url.
- No `package.json`/lockfile present → no `vulnerable-dependency`.
- No hardcoded secrets, no SQL/templates/commands/deserialization/CORS/prototype sinks present.
